sentences.en: Ten years ago, Clementine Spillur moved to Paris, France.
sentences.zh: 十年前，克莱门汀·斯皮勒搬到了法国巴黎。

sentences.en: She was full of ideas of what her life could be.
sentences.zh: 她对自己的生活充满了憧憬。

sentences.en: I just wanted to go to Paris.
I didn't really want to study anymore.
So I just packed a bag and moved to Paris, which is a pretty romantic, movie-like kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 所以我收拾好行李就搬到了巴黎，这听起来既浪漫又像电影里的情节。

sentences.en: So I guess I had this idea that you can make it in Paris.
sentences.zh: 我想我当时觉得，你可以在巴黎闯出一番天地。

sentences.en: You can just get there and then try to make it.
sentences.zh: 你只要到了那里，然后试着去打拼就行。

sentences.en: Clementine was working for a wealthy family.
sentences.zh: 克莱门汀当时为一户富裕人家工作。

sentences.en: She babysat their 11-year-old twins, cooked dinner, and cleaned a bit.
sentences.zh: 她负责照顾他们11岁的双胞胎，做晚饭，还要打扫卫生。

sentences.en: At the time, I was Clementine's neighbor.
sentences.zh: 当时，我是克莱门汀的邻居。
那是制片人让·博伊西克。

sentences.en: She grew up near Nantes, a city on the west of France.
sentences.zh: 她在法国西部城市南特附近长大。

sentences.en: Clementine stayed in the area during her undergrad, but then she wanted to see the big city.
sentences.zh: 克莱门汀在读本科期间一直待在那儿，但后来她想去大城市看看。

sentences.en: In France, Paris is the center of everything.
sentences.zh: 在法国，巴黎是所有事物的中心。

sentences.en: In exchange, the family gave her an apartment to live in.
sentences.zh: 作为交换，那家人提供给她一间公寓居住。

sentences.en: There was an interview, and then we got out of the building and walked to another building that was like two, three minutes away.
sentences.zh: 面试之后，我们离开了那栋楼，步行去了两三分钟路程外的另一栋楼。

sentences.en: And then, yeah, she took me to the room, and she was like, ta-da, that's it.
sentences.zh: 然后，是的，她带我进了房间，说：“当当！就是这儿。”

sentences.en: Clementine stared into her new home and discovered it was really small.
sentences.zh: 克莱门汀凝视着她的新家，发现它真的非常小。

sentences.en: Actually, it was just one room.
sentences.zh: 实际上，它只有一个房间。

sentences.en: There was nowhere else to sit on.
sentences.zh: 没有其他地方可以坐了。

sentences.en: There was a tiny, tiny kitchen in the corner.
sentences.zh: 角落里有一个极小的厨房。

sentences.en: There was a table that folded that I basically never used because if you unfolded it, you couldn't walk.
sentences.zh: 还有一张折叠桌，我基本没用过，因为一旦展开，你就没法走路了。

sentences.en: Basically, I think you could walk three steps in the room from the door to the window.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我觉得从门口走到窗户，房间里只能走三步。

sentences.en: In terms of widths, it was like maybe like two meters wide.
sentences.zh: 宽度方面，大概只有两米左右。

sentences.en: I remember when I was sitting on your bed, I could put my foot against the wall.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时坐在你床上时，我的脚都能抵到墙上。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a good thing I was smaller than you were because, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，幸好我比你瘦小，不然的话……

sentences.en: Clementine was living out a rite of passage for generations of young people moving to the French capital.
sentences.zh: 克莱门汀正在经历一代又一代搬到法国首都的年轻人必经的成人礼。

sentences.en: Her place was a very specific, very Parisian type of apartment called a chambre de bon, literally a maid's room.
sentences.zh: 她的住处是一种非常独特、非常巴黎式的公寓，叫“女佣房”（chambre de bonne），字面意思就是女仆的房间。

sentences.en: A chambre de bon is usually one small room on the top floor of a five or six-story apartment building.
sentences.zh: “女佣房”通常是五六层公寓楼顶层的一个小房间。

sentences.en: I lived in a chambre de bon down the hall from Clementine, but my chambre de bon was a little bigger.
sentences.zh: 我曾住在克莱门汀走廊尽头的女佣房里，但我的房间稍微大一点。

sentences.en: My apartment had two windows and my own bathroom, but it was still very small.
sentences.zh: 我的公寓有两个窗户，还有独立的浴室，但依然非常小。

sentences.en: I had a bathroom so narrow, I could stretch out my arms and touch both walls at the same time.
sentences.zh: 我的浴室窄到我伸开双臂就能同时摸到两边的墙。

sentences.en: Last October, Clementine and I returned to our old building for the first time in years to take a trip down memory lane.
sentences.zh: 去年十月，克莱门汀和我时隔多年第一次回到我们的旧楼，重温往昔。

sentences.en: That the stairs on the last one are higher.
sentences.zh: 最后那几层楼梯特别高。

sentences.en: And it's the moment when you run out of breath and you're like, I hate my life.
sentences.zh: 那是你爬到气喘吁吁，心想“我讨厌我的生活”的那一刻。

sentences.en: And you have to keep going in and you don't find it in the beginning.
sentences.zh: 你得一直往上爬，刚开始还找不到路。

sentences.en: Yeah, but I remember like climbing the stairs and seeing all the floors.
sentences.zh: 是啊，但我记得爬楼梯时看着每一层楼的样子。

sentences.en: I also remember the old guy.
Clementine lived in her chambre de bon for three years.
sentences.zh: 克莱门汀在她的女佣房里住了三年。

sentences.en: At the time, Clementine loved her apartment.
sentences.zh: 当时，克莱门汀很喜欢她的公寓。

sentences.en: It was a way to make her dream of living in Paris a reality, even though her employer felt a little awkward about it.
sentences.zh: 尽管雇主对此感到有些尴尬，但这却是她实现巴黎生活梦想的一种方式。

sentences.en: I remember she was like kind of apologizing.
sentences.zh: 我记得她当时有点像是在道歉。

sentences.en: She was kind of, sorry, that's it.
sentences.zh: 她有点不好意思地说：“抱歉，就是这样。”

sentences.en: I hope it works for you.
And me, I was just like, wow, I want to be this person.
sentences.zh: 而我当时心想，哇，我想成为这样的人。

sentences.en: Like this is, this is like you're under the roof in Paris and it's my home.
sentences.zh: 就像是，这就是巴黎屋檐下的生活，这是我的家。

sentences.en: Just like Clementine, I loved my chambre de bon.
sentences.zh: 和克莱门汀一样，我也很喜欢我的女佣房。

sentences.en: Our building was in Le Marais, a fancy neighborhood in the center of Paris, in a beautiful building hidden behind a big, heavy green door and a pretty courtyard.
sentences.zh: 我们的楼位于玛黑区，那是巴黎市中心的一个高档街区，藏在一扇厚重的大绿门和漂亮的庭院后面。

sentences.en: But today, both of us see things very differently.
sentences.zh: 但今天，我们俩对事物的看法大不相同。

sentences.en: It was kind of terrible to live in this place.
sentences.zh: 住在这个地方简直是一种折磨。

sentences.en: I remember when I moved out, I felt how my mind was able to expand as well.
sentences.zh: 我记得搬走的时候，我感觉到自己的思维也随之开阔了。

sentences.en: When I moved out, I realized that I hadn't had enough space to think.
sentences.zh: 搬走后我才意识到，我之前没有足够的空间去思考。

sentences.en: It's like the space was so small that you couldn't even get out of your own limitations mentally.
sentences.zh: 就像空间太小了，你甚至无法在精神上摆脱自己的局限。

sentences.en: It also impacts your ability to think forward and it really, living in such a tiny space is always a reminder, even if it's unconscious,
sentences.zh: 它也会影响你向前思考的能力，住在这么狭小的空间里，总是在提醒你，即使是潜意识里的，

sentences.en: that you're only entitled to this tiny bit of space.
sentences.zh: 你只配拥有这么一点点空间。

sentences.en: Parisians like Clementine have difficult relationships with the chambre de bon because it represents a lot of things.
sentences.zh: 像克莱门汀这样的巴黎人与“女佣房”有着复杂的关系，因为它代表了很多东西。

sentences.en: It's affordable housing in a city where finding housing is nearly impossible, but it's unpleasant for people who have to live there.
sentences.zh: 在住房极其难找的城市里，它是负担得起的住所，但对于必须住在那里的人来说，它并不舒适。

sentences.en: And it represents the gap between the rich people in Paris and everyone else.
sentences.zh: 它也代表了巴黎富人与其他所有人之间的鸿沟。

sentences.en: And even now that I understand the class relationship and the fact that it was so small and it's pretty violent to make people live in such small spaces.
sentences.zh: 即使现在我理解了阶级关系，也明白它太小了，让人住在这么小的空间里其实挺残忍的。

sentences.en: Today, many people live in chambre de bon apartments because there's not a lot of small, affordable housing in Paris.
sentences.zh: 今天，许多人仍住在女佣房里，因为巴黎缺乏小型、经济适用房。

sentences.en: And the city is so dense, it's impossible to build new housing.
sentences.zh: 而且城市密度太高，根本无法新建住房。

sentences.en: So the chambre de bon is an imperfect solution.
sentences.zh: 所以女佣房是一个不完美的解决方案。

sentences.en: But today, the chambre de bon are disappearing and many are wondering, where are those people going to live?
sentences.zh: 但如今，女佣房正在消失，许多人都在问：这些人以后住哪儿呢？

sentences.en: The chambre de bon was invented as a housing type during a major redesign of Paris in the 1850s.
sentences.zh: 女佣房作为一种住房类型，是在19世纪50年代巴黎大改造期间发明的。

sentences.en: It was led by a man named Georges-Eugène Haussmann, whose name I will pronounce the English way.
sentences.zh: 这项工程由乔治-欧仁·奥斯曼领导，我会用英语发音他的名字。

sentences.en: Yeah, I don't know how to say it that way.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我不知道怎么用那种发音说。

sentences.en: Anyway, Haussmann was the prefect for Paris for 20 years.
sentences.zh: 总之，奥斯曼担任巴黎行政长官长达20年。

sentences.en: He was commissioned by Emperor Napoleon III to overhaul the city's architecture.
sentences.zh: 他受拿破仑三世皇帝委托，对城市的建筑进行了彻底改造。

sentences.en: Napoleon wanted Paris to be masterful and a capital of the world.
sentences.zh: 拿破仑希望巴黎成为宏伟的世界之都。

sentences.en: To reflect these grand ambitions, Haussmann created wide boulevards and avenues.
sentences.zh: 为了体现这些宏大的抱负，奥斯曼修建了宽阔的林荫大道和街道。

sentences.en: A lot of people say Haussmann made the bourgeoisie visible in Paris.
sentences.zh: 很多人说奥斯曼让资产阶级在巴黎变得显眼起来。

sentences.en: He destroyed working-class neighborhoods and replaced them with luxury buildings.
sentences.zh: 他摧毁了工人阶级社区，取而代之的是豪华建筑。

sentences.en: Paris was a mess of construction for 50 years.
sentences.zh: 巴黎有50年时间都处于混乱的施工状态。

sentences.en: Workers from all over the country came to serve Haussmann's vision.
sentences.zh: 来自全国各地的工人们来到这里，为实现奥斯曼的愿景服务。

sentences.en: Suddenly, in the streets of Paris, you could hear accents and songs sung by workers from all over France.
sentences.zh: 突然间，在巴黎的街道上，你可以听到来自法国各地工人的口音和歌声。

sentences.en: They created some of Paris' most iconic landmarks.
sentences.zh: 他们创造了巴黎一些最具标志性的地标。

sentences.en: The Avenue de l'Opéra, the Boulevard Haussmann, the Boulevard Voltaire.
sentences.zh: 歌剧院大街、奥斯曼大道、伏尔泰大道。

sentences.en: But all this construction was at a coSt.
sentences.zh: 但所有这些建设都是有代价的。

sentences.en: In some cases, Haussmann cut buildings in half to make room for new ones.
sentences.zh: 在某些情况下，奥斯曼将建筑一分为二，为新建筑腾出空间。

sentences.en: Some people called him an artist demolisher.
sentences.zh: 有些人称他为“拆迁艺术家”。

sentences.en: Haussmann only designed apartments because that's where everyone lived in Paris at the time.
sentences.zh: 奥斯曼只设计公寓，因为当时巴黎所有人都住在公寓里。

sentences.en: And he designed every apartment building to be the same, inside and out.
sentences.zh: 而且他设计的每一栋公寓楼在内外结构上都是一样的。
她是一位建筑历史学家。

sentences.en: Marie-Jeanne says in Haussmann's buildings, there was always one apartment per floor.
sentences.zh: 玛丽-珍妮说，在奥斯曼的建筑中，每层楼通常只有一套公寓。

sentences.en: And in those luxury buildings, the families expected to have rooms to house their servants.
sentences.zh: 而在那些豪华公寓里，家庭成员期望有专门的房间来安置仆人。

sentences.en: In the 1850s, during the Haussmann redesign of Paris, there was a large influx of young women moving to the city to work for the bourgeoisie.
sentences.zh: 19世纪50年代，在奥斯曼改造巴黎期间，大量年轻女性涌入城市，为资产阶级工作。

sentences.en: They came from poor regions like Brittany in the west of France.
sentences.zh: 她们来自法国西部布列塔尼等贫困地区。

sentences.en: At the time, French regions were mostly rural.
sentences.zh: 当时，法国各地区大多是农村。

sentences.en: And coming to Paris was a way to find a job and send money to your family.
sentences.zh: 来到巴黎是寻找工作并寄钱回家的途径。

sentences.en: All those people who came were quite young, 14 or 15 years old in many cases.
sentences.zh: 所有来的人都很年轻，很多只有14或15岁。

sentences.en: Life was hard for these servants, and many of them were living inside their employers' apartments,
sentences.zh: 这些仆人的生活很艰难，许多人住在雇主的公寓里，

sentences.en: which made them available to work 24 hours a day with very few breaks.
sentences.zh: 这使得她们必须24小时待命，几乎没有休息时间。

sentences.en: In 19th century France, it was common for rich French people to wake up their servants in the middle of the night
sentences.zh: 在19世纪的法国，富人半夜叫醒仆人是很常见的，

sentences.en: for small, annoying tasks like fetching a glass of water.
sentences.zh: 只是为了像倒杯水这样琐碎又烦人的小事。

sentences.en: The work ruined many of these young workers, who returned home after life in Paris, exhausted and demoralized.
sentences.zh: 这种工作摧毁了许多年轻工人的身心，她们在巴黎生活后回到家乡时，往往精疲力竭且意志消沉。

sentences.en: Marie-Jeanne is explaining that before the Chambre de Bonne, in the 18th century,
sentences.zh: 玛丽-珍妮解释说，在18世纪“女佣房”出现之前，

sentences.en: servants lived in areas above the kitchen or the stables.
sentences.zh: 仆人们住在厨房或马厩上方的区域。

sentences.en: Chambermaids would sleep in tiny rooms near the employer's bedroom.
sentences.zh: 女仆们会睡在雇主卧室附近的小房间里。

sentences.en: Very small rooms, usually with no window.
sentences.zh: 非常小的房间，通常没有窗户。

sentences.en: But the Haussmann redesign changed that.
sentences.zh: 但奥斯曼的改造改变了这一点。

sentences.en: Marie-Jeanne says, before Haussmann, Paris apartment buildings had small triangle roofs made of zinc.
sentences.zh: 玛丽-珍妮说，在奥斯曼之前，巴黎的公寓楼有锌制的小三角屋顶。

sentences.en: There was not a lot of room to install an attic under the roofs,
sentences.zh: 屋顶下没有多少空间可以安装阁楼，

sentences.en: but Haussmann's redesign included a series of sloped, mansard roofs.
sentences.zh: 但奥斯曼的改造包括了一系列倾斜的“曼萨德”屋顶。

sentences.en: The mansard roofs were sweeping and dramatic.
sentences.zh: 曼萨德屋顶宽阔而引人注目。

sentences.en: But Haussmann created these sloped roofs because of something very mundane, municipal height restrictions.
sentences.zh: 但奥斯曼设计这些斜屋顶是因为一个非常世俗的原因：市政高度限制。

sentences.en: At the time, Paris had a height limit on new buildings.
sentences.zh: 当时，巴黎对新建筑有高度限制。

sentences.en: Every building could only be 65 feet tall.
sentences.zh: 每栋建筑最高只能有65英尺。

sentences.en: But that height limit wasn't for the very top of the building.
sentences.zh: 但这个高度限制不是针对建筑的最顶端。

sentences.en: It was for the cornice line, where the roof begins.
sentences.zh: 而是针对檐口线，即屋顶开始的地方。

sentences.en: So the mansard roof is kind of like cheating.
sentences.zh: 所以曼萨德屋顶算是一种“作弊”。

sentences.en: It allowed the building to be taller without violating city laws.
sentences.zh: 它允许建筑在不违反城市法规的情况下变得更高。

sentences.en: Now, the very top floors were all big triangles,
sentences.zh: 现在，最顶层全是巨大的三角形空间，

sentences.en: and they could put big attics under there.
sentences.zh: 他们可以在下面安装大阁楼。

sentences.en: These triangle attics weren't desirable for the bourgeoisie living in Paris.
sentences.zh: 这些三角形阁楼对于住在巴黎的资产阶级来说并不理想。

sentences.en: You could not rent it out like the rest of the apartment.
sentences.zh: 你无法像公寓的其他部分那样把它租出去。

sentences.en: But the bourgeoisie decided that they would pay a little extra money for the space
sentences.zh: 但资产阶级决定，他们愿意为这个空间多付一点钱，

sentences.en: and put their servants up there.
That's how the idea of the Chambre de Bonne was born.
sentences.zh: 这就是“女佣房”概念的诞生过程。

sentences.en: Instead of living with their employers,
now maids and servants could live in a private space above them.
sentences.zh: 现在女佣和仆人们可以住在他们上方的一个私人空间里。

sentences.en: I visited a typical, classic Chambre de Bonne with Marie-Jeanne Dumont.
sentences.zh: 我和玛丽-珍妮·杜蒙参观了一间典型、经典的女佣房。

sentences.en: This apartment is in the 11th arrondissement, right near La Place de la République.
sentences.zh: 这间公寓位于第11区，就在共和国广场附近。

sentences.en: Marie-Jeanne is telling me that this Chambre de Bonne was pretty typical of its era.
sentences.zh: 玛丽-珍妮告诉我，这间女佣房在那个时代非常典型。

sentences.en: It was lit up by a small window.
The space is very well preserved.
sentences.zh: 这个空间保存得非常好。

sentences.en: It actually looks like it came straight from the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 看起来就像直接从19世纪保留下来的一样。

sentences.en: Marie-Jeanne says that Chambre de Bonne were by definition very small.
sentences.zh: 玛丽-珍妮说，女佣房从定义上讲就非常小。

sentences.en: So, architects had to make the most of every square foot of space.
sentences.zh: 所以，建筑师必须充分利用每一平方英尺的空间。

sentences.en: This old-style Chambre de Bonne is a lot smaller than the one I lived in.
sentences.zh: 这种老式的女佣房比我住的那间要小得多。

sentences.en: Based on Hausmann's designs, the original Chambre de Bonne were usually about 75 square feet.
sentences.zh: 根据奥斯曼的设计，最初的女佣房通常只有约75平方英尺。

sentences.en: You could barely fit a bed in there.
sentences.zh: 那里几乎连一张床都放不下。

sentences.en: It was typical for these rooms to have one iron bed,
sentences.zh: 这些房间通常只配有一张铁床、

sentences.en: a small table, a chair, and a small piece of furniture to store things.
sentences.zh: 一张小桌子、一把椅子，还有一件用来存放物品的小家具。

sentences.en: The only bathrooms or sinks were in the hallway.
sentences.zh: 唯一的浴室或水槽都在走廊里。

sentences.en: The early Chambre de Bonne were not well maintained by the rich people.
sentences.zh: 早期的“女仆房”并没有得到富人们的妥善维护。

sentences.en: Some bourgeois didn't even change the sheets when they hired new employees.
sentences.zh: 有些资产阶级在雇佣新员工时，甚至连床单都不换。
那里的生活简直糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: Domestic workers would die because there was no ventilation.
sentences.zh: 家政工人们常因缺乏通风而丧命。

sentences.en: At the beginning of the 20th century,
Parisians became very concerned about tuberculosis.
sentences.zh: 巴黎人开始非常担心肺结核问题。

sentences.en: They started to believe that the Chambre de Bonnes were so filthy,
sentences.zh: 他们开始认为“女仆房”太脏了，

sentences.en: and that the maids brought the diseases into their employer's home.
sentences.zh: 而且女仆会把疾病带进雇主的家里。

sentences.en: So, the very first Chambre de Bonne were abandoned,
sentences.zh: 于是，最初的那些“女仆房”被废弃了，

sentences.en: and employers moved servants into slightly bigger rooMs.
